info.title: Human Service API
info.description: Scrapes and caches a person's online presence (websites, LinkedIn, blog, etc.) to provide writing context for AI content generation.

provider.description: Lead provider. apollo/apify are the searchable people-gateway providers; crm is a client's uploaded contact list (served via an audience's serve-next, not searchable here).

total.description: Total matchable. apify: pipelinelabs-only signal (provider cursor, not a cross-source-exact total).

nextOffset.description: apify offset for the next page (null when done / apollo cursor-based).

timezone.description: Recipient's IANA timezone (e.g. 'America/New_York'), threaded from the provider so downstream send-scheduling lands in the prospect's local business hours. null when the provider omits it.

businessLanguages.description: Language(s) this person plausibly conducts business in, as ISO 639-1 codes (e.g. 'de', 'fr', 'it'). ORDERED, most plausible first — the ordering is a guarantee, consumers may select by position (index 0 = the single most plausible business language). An EMPTY array means UNKNOWN: we had no usable signal and deliberately do not fabricate one, which is distinct from ['en'] (= known to be English). Derived from the person's own city/state/country, falling back to their organization's; region beats country wherever a country is genuinely multilingual (Swiss cantons, Belgian regions, Canadian provinces).

provider.description: Lead provider. apollo/apify are the searchable people-gateway providers; crm is a client's uploaded contact list (served via an audience's serve-next, not searchable here).

providerPersonId.description: apollo person id (usable for a later enrich). null for apify.

employmentHistory.description: The person's FULL career history as the provider serves it — every role, in provider order (the ordering is part of the contract). `current: true` marks the role the provider flags as current. null when the provider serves no history; it is never reconstructed from the top-level organization.

phone.description: The person's phone number in E.164 (e.g. '+33612345678'), as the provider holds it — what a phone channel (WhatsApp, SMS) writes to. ABSENT when the provider holds none: only crm-service serves one today (its contact's phoneE164), so apollo / apify persons never carry the key.

providerOrganizationId.description: The provider's own organization id. null when the provider serves none.

keywords.description: The organization's keywords as the provider serves them, in provider order. null means the provider served none — which is NOT the same claim as an empty list.

technologyNames.description: The organization's technology stack by name, in provider order. null when the provider serves none.

annualRevenuePrinted.description: Human-readable annual revenue as the provider printed it (e.g. '$12.4M'). The numeric form is `annualRevenue`.

fundingEvents.description: Every funding round the provider serves, in provider order. null when it serves none.

occurredOn.description: Day the signal happened (YYYY-MM-DD), as the provider recorded it.

fact.description: One English sentence stating the signal, for the email writer to reference.
fact.example: Acme Clinics posted a job for Office Manager (Austin, United States) on September 21, 2026

sourceUrl.description: The posting or news link when the provider gives one.

BuyingSignal.description: The buying signal this person's audience matched (the company is hiring, the person just changed jobs, the company just raised), with its date and a one-line fact the email writer can reference. Present only on a revealed person served from a buying-signal audience; null otherwise (free search teasers, apify, crm, and any person the provider holds no dated evidence for). Never defaulted or invented.

competitorPage.description: The competitor LinkedIn company page whose post the person engaged with.

postPublishedOn.description: Approximate day the post was published (YYYY-MM-DD); LinkedIn only gives a relative age.

LinkedinEngagementEvidence.description: linkedin_engagement only (absent on the other kinds): the competitor post this person reacted to or commented on. It explains WHY this person was chosen; it is never material for the message, which must not mention it.

provider.description: Lead provider. apollo/apify are the searchable people-gateway providers; crm is a client's uploaded contact list (served via an audience's serve-next, not searchable here).

need.description: Intent routing: 'verified_email' routes to apify. Ignored if `provider` is set.

nextPage.description: apollo only: omit filters and advance the server-managed cursor for the next page.

limit.description: apify only: max leads to return (provider cap 1000). Defaults to 1 — apify bills per returned lead (each hit carries a verified email; no free teaser list), so the gateway takes the strict minimum unless you consciously raise it to batch.

offset.description: apify only: pagination offset (pass back `nextOffset` from the prior page).

audienceId.description: Tag returned (served) leads as members of this audience (provenance membership). The audience must belong to the org (404 otherwise). Tagging applies to billed serves only — apify search hits (every hit is billed). Does not change which filters are searched; the caller supplies filters as usual.

functions.description: Job functions. Honored by apify only — apollo has no functions search filter.

companyNames.description: Company names. Honored by apify only — apollo searches by domain/industry, not name.

technologies.description: Tech stack. apify + apollo (apollo technology UIDs).

provider.description: Lead provider. apollo/apify are the searchable people-gateway providers; crm is a client's uploaded contact list (served via an audience's serve-next, not searchable here).
Defaults to apollo (same as search). Set 'apify' for the verified-email waterfall. The reveal follows the provider that searched — a provider person id only means something to its own provider.

providerPersonId.description: apollo only: the apollo person id returned by a prior search. Reveals the verified email via apollo /enrich (the billed path, 1 credit). PREFERRED for apollo — apollo search masks last name + domain, so identity-based match can't be satisfied from a search hit.

includeInferred.description: apify only: include pattern-inferred emails in the waterfall.

failedSegments.description: Retained for response-shape stability (the split returns later). Layer 1 emits ONE audience today, so a failed build FAILS the request LOUD (502 carrying the underlying reason) rather than returning an empty list — this array is therefore always empty on a 200.

audienceId.description: The id of the PERSISTED audience row (status 'suggested', inactive). The caller activates a chosen candidate via PATCH /orgs/audiences/{id}/status {status:'active'}.

name.description: Short human label for this audience (<=4 words), shared across providers — the layer-1 name.

rationale.description: One-sentence description of who this audience targets.

provider.description: Always 'apollo' — apollo-service owns the faithful filters; the candidate commits to apollo.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience apollo-service built + persisted for this audience.

filters.description: The faithful Apollo filter object (opaque — apollo-service owns its shape), cached on the persisted audience row.

count.description: The audience's live match count (free apollo dry-run snapshot from apollo-service).

validationError.description: Retained for response-shape stability. apollo-service confirms a real audience (or fails loud), so always null.

truncated.description: Reserved for response compatibility. Layer 1 has no hard cap, so freshly suggested candidates return false.

degraded.description: The chooser's verdict: true when NO attempt apollo-service explored really answered the request and it picked the least-bad one anyway. INFORMATION only — a degraded audience is served, persisted and activatable exactly like any other; the customer decides whether to keep it. A candidate is always returned; this never withholds one.

name.description: The layer-1 audience name that failed to build.

reason.description: The underlying error message (apollo-service build or chooser failure).

nlPrompt.description: Natural-language audience description. Layer 1 restates it as ONE audience — the request is never split (the split is deferred to the post-validation A/B-split step). The response is still a list: an array of one.

offerId.description: Optional offer this batch of candidates is assembled for (brand-service owns the offer entity; stored opaquely, never resolved here). Every persisted candidate carries it, so GET /orgs/audiences?offerId= returns them. Omitted ⟹ brand-wide, byte-identical to the pre-offer behaviour.

description.description: One-sentence summary of who THIS audience targets, distinct from the shared batch nlPrompt. LLM-generated at /suggest time. null for rows predating this field.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience owned by apollo-service ('one filter vocabulary' Wave 2). Set for apollo audiences; null for apify (legacy) rows and pre-Wave-2 rows not yet backfilled. The faithful filters live in apollo-service; the `filters` field below is human-service's opaque cache of them.

crmUploadId.description: The ONE imported CRM source (crm-service upload id) this audience is bound to. When set, every CRM serve made under this audience is restricted to the people that came from that file, so several CRM audiences can coexist for one brand and each behaves as its own audience. null = unbound ⟹ the serve covers the brand's whole imported list (the pre-existing behaviour).

segment.description: A part of the brand's own CRM, as crm-service's PeopleSegment states it (passed through verbatim, validated by crm-service): dealStages [{stage, pipeline?}], dealStatuses, tags, reached / notReached (funnel steps), includeClients, includeOptedOut. Lists OR, keys AND; clients and opted-out people are out unless stated. Names come from crm-service GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

crmPeople.description: The PEOPLE-pool filter this CRM audience is bound to: every serve draws from the brand's merged people (everyone its connected tools know, one row per human) who match it, instead of from imported files. null = not people-bound (file-bound via crmUploadId, or the whole imported list).

crmPeopleByStage.description: A people-bound CRM audience whose segment names dealStages: crm-service's counts per stated stage (same snapshot as Size / Remaining). Entries overlap when a person holds deals at two of them. null otherwise.

offerId.description: The offer (Org > Brand > Offer > Campaign) this audience belongs to — an id owned by brand-service. An audience is assembled for one distinct thing the brand sells, so it is scoped to that offer rather than to every offer of the brand. null = no offer stated ⟹ the audience is brand-wide, the pre-existing behaviour.

profileAudienceId.description: The client PROFILE (WHO, a cold audience the client keeps or pauses on the Targeting page) this source list was built for: a buying-signal list (hiring now, new in role, recently funded) or a competitor-post engagement list finds THAT profile's people, screened against the profile's text. Pausing or archiving the profile pauses its lists; resuming it resumes them (unless the source itself is off). null on a profile itself, on a whole-ICP list built before profiles had their own (retired once they do), and on every other audience. Show profiles = rows with null here and channels[0].list = apollo_search; sources = channels[0].list.

canonicalAudienceId.description: When this audience is a deprecated provider-variant (e.g. retired '<base> [Apify]' from the apify->apollo migration), the id of its active canonical replacement. Membership/stats reads resolve a deprecated match to this audience. null for non-deprecated / unlinked rows.

avatarUrl.description: Audience avatar as a hosted HTTP(S) URL. null until generated.

degraded.description: The chooser's verdict on the audience it picked for this row: true when no attempt apollo-service explored really answered the request and the least-bad one was chosen anyway. INFORMATION for the customer and the dashboard — nothing here blocks, filters or warns on it, and an audience is always chosen. false for rows created before the flag existed and whenever the chooser judged the pick a genuine answer.

targetText.description: THE text of this audience: who the customer wants for THIS audience, in plain language. It is the text to show as the audience AND the text the pre-pay screen (Jev) judges every lead of every list below against, before any paid reveal. Distinct from nlPrompt, which a split shares across all its sibling audiences. null ⟹ see targetTextMissingReason.

targetTextOrigin.description: How targetText was written. segment_target: this audience is one of several split from one shared target, and the text was drafted for this audience alone from that target + its own segment. audience_target: the audience is not one of several, so its nlPrompt IS its text. null when targetText is null.

targetTextMissingReason.description: Why targetText is null. no_customer_text: the audience holds no customer text at all (no nlPrompt), so there is nothing to judge leads against. not_written_yet: the text is being drafted (it is written before the audience's first serve; until then the screen judges against nlPrompt and records that it did). null when targetText is set.

channels.description: WHERE this audience's people are found: its own list first, then one entry per SOURCE of the audience (a buying signal, competitor-post engagement), each with its own size. A source is never an audience of its own. Every lead from every list is screened against targetText before it is used. Empty for an audience with no committed provider.

channel.description: The outreach channel that uses this list. cold_email is the only channel today.

list.description: What the list is. apollo_search: an Apollo people search. apollo_buying_signal: the same search narrowed to people showing a buying signal (see signal). linkedin_engagement: people who engaged with competitor LinkedIn posts (see signal). crm_contacts: the client's own uploaded contacts. apify_search: legacy search provider.

audienceId.description: The audience this list finds people for (always the audience itself).

sourceId.description: Set on a SOURCE of the audience (a buying signal, competitor-post engagement): WHERE its people are also looked for, beside its own list. Absent on the audience's own list (the first entry).

name.description: The source's name (e.g. "Hiring now"). Absent on the own list.

status.description: A source's on/off (its source campaign). Absent on the own list.

signal.description: The buying signal that narrows the list, with its rolling window. null for a plain list.

size.description: How many people the list holds. On the audiences LIST it is the same figure as the row's sizeCount. null ⟹ see sizeUnknownReason.

sizeUnknownReason.description: Why size is null. not_built_yet: the list's Apollo filters are still being built. unknown_until_walked: no provider count exists for this kind (linkedin_engagement) until serving walks the whole list. not_counted: a CRM list, whose size the provider does not report here.

provider.description: The provider this audience commits to. apollo/apify when persisting a candidate from /suggest; crm for a brand whose audience is its uploaded contact list (served by crm-service — no filters/apolloAudienceId, brand-scoped). Omit for a neutral audience.

apolloAudienceId.description: Pointer to the faithful Apollo audience owned by apollo-service, when persisting an apollo candidate. Omit for a neutral / apify audience.

crmUploadId.description: Bind this audience to ONE imported CRM source (a crm-service upload id of the same brand). Every CRM serve made under this audience is then restricted to the people of that file, so several bound audiences can coexist for one brand and each is independently pausable + independently costed. Validated against the brand's uploads at creation (400 if it is not one of them). Omit to keep the whole-brand behaviour. Immutable afterwards.

offerId.description: The offer this audience belongs to — a brand-service offer id. Scopes the audience to one distinct thing the brand sells; name uniqueness becomes per (org, brand, offer), so two offers of the same brand may each own an audience with the same name. Stored as-is: human-service defines no offer semantics and does not resolve the id (same as brandId). Omit to keep the brand-wide behaviour. Immutable afterwards.

apolloCount.description: Optional count snapshot the caller already obtained from /orgs/people/search/dry-run (apollo). Stored as-is; refresh-count re-computes it server-side later. Accepts null (e.g. an apify-source candidate carries apolloCount: null).

apifyCount.description: Optional apify count snapshot (see apolloCount). Accepts null (e.g. an apollo-source candidate carries apifyCount: null).

signedUp.description: true = only people who signed up to the brand's product (a signup on its auth provider); false = only people who did not.

replied.description: false = only people who NEVER wrote to the brand on any conversation channel (email, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, an answer to our outreach); true = only people who did.

reachableBy.description: Only people holding a phone / an email. A phone channel (WhatsApp, SMS) wants 'phone': a person served without one is burned for nothing.

segment.description: A part of the brand's own CRM, as crm-service's PeopleSegment states it (passed through verbatim, validated by crm-service): dealStages [{stage, pipeline?}], dealStatuses, tags, reached / notReached (funnel steps), includeClients, includeOptedOut. Lists OR, keys AND; clients and opted-out people are out unless stated. Names come from crm-service GET /orgs/contacts/segments.

CrmPeopleFilter.description: Bind this CRM audience to the brand's merged PEOPLE matching a filter (e.g. {signedUp: true, replied: false} = product signups who never answered) instead of to an imported file, optionally scoped to a `segment` of the brand's own CRM (e.g. {segment: {dealStages: [{pipeline: 'Sales Pipeline', stage: 'Form Filled - No Appointment'}]}}). Requires provider 'crm'; exclusive with crmUploadId. A segment crm-service refuses is a 400 carrying its reason. Every serve passes the filter to crm-service (same brand-wide no-re-serve forever); each served person carries its phone when crm-service holds one. Validated against crm-service's serve-stats at creation (its counts become the audience's Size / Remaining). Immutable afterwards.

offerId.description: The brand-service offer this audience belongs to. Stored verbatim, like brandId. Omitted = brand-wide.

name.description: Audience name (English), unique per (brand, offer). Omitted = apollo-service's label (competitor slugs + window).

nlPrompt.description: Who among the engagers is worth writing to, in plain English (people, not only companies). Stored as the audience target: the pre-pay screen judges every engager teaser (name, title, headline, employer) against it before any email is paid for.

windowDays.description: Age of the competitor posts whose engagers are served, in days, counted back from each serve (rolling).

competitorPages.description: 1-3 competitor LinkedIn company page URLs (https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>/). Validated by apollo-service, whose named 400 is relayed.

filters.description: Apollo base filters. Must be empty: apollo-service refuses Apollo filters beside this signal with a named 400 (relayed), since its people are LinkedIn engagers, not an Apollo search. Omitted = {}.

sizeCount.description: Total contactable audience pool = the committed provider's count snapshot (apollo -> apolloCount, apify -> apifyCount) MINUS the people the pre-pay screen judged off target for this audience. Those people are provably not in the audience, so they leave the pool itself, not only the remaining-to-contact count. 0 for a never-counted audience. ABSENT (with availableToContactCount / availableToContactPct) for a linkedin_engagement audience whose pool is unknown: no provider count exists for it until serve-next has walked it to exhaustion, after which it is that walked pool.

availableToContactCount.description: Pool members NOT suppressed within the 3-month re-contact window (never-served, or last served >3 months ago). Computed server-side from the same per-brand cross-provider suppression the serve path enforces.

availableToContactPct.description: round(availableToContactCount / sizeCount * 100), integer 0..100. 0 when sizeCount is 0. Denominator is exactly sizeCount so Size and Remaining stay coherent.

provenance.description: 'served' when any membership resolving to this audience was a serve, else 'found_taken'.

status.description: ready = real rows below. empty = the provider's search matched nobody (reason no_match); final for this audience. unavailable = no sample can be taken right now: reason not_built_yet (the audience's provider-side filters are still being built; ask again shortly) or provider_not_previewable (a CRM-upload or retired apify audience has no free search to sample).

matchCount.description: The provider's live match count (people with a verified email) at the moment the sample was taken. Null when unavailable.

peopleInSample.description: How many of the provider's first page of matching people work there. A share of the sample, not a headcount.

companies.description: Up to ~10 real employers of people who match the audience, in the provider's order. Name only: descriptors (domain, industry, size) would need a paid company search.

lastNameObfuscated.description: Masked by the provider's free search, e.g. "Ni***s".

company.description: Always one of the listed companies.

people.description: Up to ~20 real people who match the audience, as the provider's free search serves them. Never an email, a phone, a location or a photo.

generatedAt.description: When the sample was taken (ISO 8601). Null when unavailable.

status.description: ready = `people` below. unavailable = no check can run for this audience; see `reason`.

reason.description: Why unavailable. The preview's own reasons (no_match, not_built_yet: ask again shortly, provider_not_previewable), empty_sample (the preview holds no people), no_reveal_handle (the provider did not identify the sampled people, so none can be revealed).

done.description: True when every checked person is settled (found or not_found), or when unavailable. Stop calling /next.

index.description: Position of this person in the preview's `people` array.

status.description: pending = not attempted yet. checking = a reveal is running now (another call). found = an email came back. not_found = the finder ran and returned no email.

finder.description: The finder that ran (today always "apollo"). Null until settled.

verifier.description: The verifier that judged the found address, as the provider names it (e.g. "bounceverify"). Null unless found.

verdict.description: The verifier's verdict on the found address. Null unless found.

deliverable.description: True only for verdict valid. Null unless found.

maskedEmail.description: The found address's domain behind a masked local part, e.g. "***@acme.com". The address itself is never returned.

checkedAt.description: When the outcome came back (ISO 8601). Null until settled.

people.description: The first few people of the preview (at most 5), in preview order. Only real attempts and real outcomes: nothing is marked found or not_found until the finder answered.

status.description: ready = rows below (possibly more to page). empty = the audience matched nobody (reason no_match). unavailable = reason not_built_yet (ask again shortly) or provider_not_previewable (CRM-upload / retired apify audience).

index.description: Stable 0-based rank of the company in this audience's list. Never changes once built.

description.description: One line, as the provider describes the company.

lastNameObfuscated.description: Masked by the provider, e.g. "Ni***s". The full name is revealed only after signup.

linkedinUrl.description: Only when the provider gives it without a reveal; usually null.

person.description: The one person of the audience to write to at this company. Never an email or a phone.

rows.description: The requested page of rows, in index order. A field the provider does not give is null, never invented.

totalAvailable.description: Rows built and stored so far for this audience (grows as callers page).

nextOffset.description: Offset of the next page; null when there is nothing more to ask for.

done.description: True once the list is complete (maxRows reached, or the audience ran out of companies).

maxCheckable.description: Only rows with index below this can be email-checked (10).

checks.description: One per built row with index < maxCheckable, in index order.

status.description: pending = not attempted yet. checking = a reveal is running now (another call). found = an email came back. not_found = the finder ran and returned no email.

finder.description: The finder that ran (today always "apollo"). Null until settled.

verifier.description: The verifier that judged the found address (e.g. "bounceverify"). Null unless found.

verdict.description: The verifier's verdict. Null unless found.

deliverable.description: True only for verdict valid. Null unless found.

maskedEmail.description: e.g. "***@acme.com". The address itself is never returned.

checkedAt.description: When the outcome came back (ISO 8601). Null until settled.

status.description: 'served' ⟹ a fresh person is returned. 'exhausted' ⟹ no new match remains for this audience within the suppression window (person is null). 'pending' ⟹ the per-call walk budget ran out before a person was found (person is null); progress is kept, so call again to continue. 'pending' is NOT exhaustion.

allOf.description: The next unserved person (real provider match on the audience's stored filters), recorded as served so the next call returns someone new. null when exhausted.

personId.description: human-service's canonical person id for the served person: the same `personId` GET /orgs/audiences/{id}/members returns for them. Durable across providers (never a provider id). Present on every 'served' answer; omitted when 'exhausted'.

reason.description: On 'exhausted' only, when it is NOT exhaustion of the pool. no_recent_posts = a linkedin_engagement audience whose competitor pages hold no post inside its window (the pages were read): the audience fills as soon as a competitor posts. Absent on every other answer.

emailVerdict.description: On 'served' only, and only when the request stated `acceptedEmails`: the verification verdict of the address handed out (valid, or catch_all when the request accepted it). null = this serve ran no verification (crm, apify). Absent when the request did not state `acceptedEmails` (that body is unchanged).

reachableBy.description: The contact channel(s) the SERVING PIPE writes on, all required (phone for WhatsApp / SMS / calls, email for email). A person without them is never served, revealed or marked served for this call, so a pipe that can reach them still gets them. crm pushes it down to crm-service; a provider whose people cannot carry it (apollo / apify: no phone) answers exhausted before any search or reveal. Omitted = unchanged.

acceptedEmails.description: Which email verification verdicts this serve may hand out, as the calling workflow states it. 'valid_only' (the default when omitted) = only an address the verifier confirmed (verdict valid, <1% bounce). 'valid_and_catch_all' = also an address on a catch-all domain (verdict catch_all, ~7% bounce), so a market that ran out of confirmed mailboxes keeps reaching people. 'valid_catch_all_and_unknown' = also an address the verifier could not judge (verdict unknown, ~15% bounce), a knowing choice. invalid and risky are never handed out, whatever the value. With 'valid_and_catch_all' (resp. 'valid_catch_all_and_unknown'), the catch-all (resp. catch-all and unknown) people this audience already revealed, verified and dropped for the brand are handed out FIRST, from what is stored: no new reveal, no new verification, no second charge, each person once, each with their own verdict. Accepted on serve-next, candidates/next and candidates/{candidateId}/reveal (send the same value on all three). Stating it (either value) also adds `emailVerdict` to every served answer. Providers without verification (crm, apify): no effect.

relationships.description: Who the SERVING PIPE may hand out, by the person's relationship with the brand (tags owned by lead-service). 'business_only' = nobody tagged personal, investor, supplier, team, partner or advisor, and nobody whose thread was never judged. Pushed down to crm-service on a CRM-sourced serve (a CRM audience, or the CRM feature identity), which decides and does NOT mark a refused person served, so another pipe still gets them. No effect on a search-provider audience (apollo / apify: strangers). Omitted = unchanged.

stepFilter.description: Which funnel steps the person reached in the brand's own tools, as the SERVING PIPE's play states it (e.g. reached a form or a meeting, never a sale, never disqualified). Vocabulary and validation are crm-service's: forwarded VERBATIM, top-level, to crm-service on every CRM-sourced serve (a CRM audience, or the CRM feature identity), ANDed there with the audience's own pool filter; crm-service refusing it is relayed as a 400, never an unfiltered serve. A search-provider audience (apollo / apify) cannot honour it: the serve is refused (422). Omitted = unchanged.

status.description: 'candidate' ⟹ a free candidate, every free check applied (brand suppression, opt-outs, won people, own company, hard bounces, people already rejected for this audience); nothing billed. 'exhausted' ⟹ none left (`reason`). 'pending' ⟹ the per-call walk budget ran out; call again.

reason.description: On 'exhausted' only. pool_exhausted = the provider has nobody new. yield_exhausted = over the last 1,000 decisions under the latest `basis`, fewer than 3 were reveals. unreachable_by_provider = the request's `reachableBy` names a channel this provider's people never carry (nothing popped or offered). no_recent_posts = a linkedin_engagement audience whose competitor pages hold no post inside its window (the pages were read): NOT exhaustion, the audience fills as soon as a competitor posts.

target.description: The audience's own text: who the client wants for THIS audience, the text the pre-pay screen judges every candidate against (`targetText`, else the shared `nlPrompt`). null when the audience has neither.

sourceId.description: The audience source that found this candidate (a buying signal, competitor-post engagement); null = the audience's own list.

offeredAt.description: ISO time the candidate was (last) offered. An undecided offer is offered again after 15 minutes.

domain.description: Employer web domain as the provider served it on the free teaser. null when the provider served none (never guessed).

status.description: 'served' ⟹ the same served person serve-next returns, recorded as served. 'not_served' ⟹ the reveal ran (billed) but nobody servable came out (no usable / deliverable email, or blocked after the reveal); ask for the next candidate.

personId.description: Canonical human-service person id, present on 'served' (same as serve-next).

emailVerdict.description: On 'served' only, and only when the request stated `acceptedEmails`: the verification verdict of the address handed out (valid, or catch_all when the request accepted it). null = this serve ran no verification (crm, apify). Absent when the request did not state `acceptedEmails` (that body is unchanged).

reason.description: On every 'not_served'. provider_skipped = the provider declined to buy the reveal (its mail domain cannot verify; NO credit spent). Every other reason comes after a bought reveal: no_person / no_email = the provider returned nobody / no address; not_deliverable = the address failed verification (see verdict); opted_out / won / already_served / own_company / bounced = a gate after the reveal. CRM candidates: email_not_found = the contact had no email and the lookup found none (or it could not be looked up), never handed out again; email_lookup_pending = the finder is still working, the candidate is offered again later (nothing billed twice).

acceptedEmails.description: Which email verification verdicts this serve may hand out, as the calling workflow states it. 'valid_only' (the default when omitted) = only an address the verifier confirmed (verdict valid, <1% bounce). 'valid_and_catch_all' = also an address on a catch-all domain (verdict catch_all, ~7% bounce), so a market that ran out of confirmed mailboxes keeps reaching people. 'valid_catch_all_and_unknown' = also an address the verifier could not judge (verdict unknown, ~15% bounce), a knowing choice. invalid and risky are never handed out, whatever the value. With 'valid_and_catch_all' (resp. 'valid_catch_all_and_unknown'), the catch-all (resp. catch-all and unknown) people this audience already revealed, verified and dropped for the brand are handed out FIRST, from what is stored: no new reveal, no new verification, no second charge, each person once, each with their own verdict. Accepted on serve-next, candidates/next and candidates/{candidateId}/reveal (send the same value on all three). Stating it (either value) also adds `emailVerdict` to every served answer. Providers without verification (crm, apify): no effect.
